programme: A Polycomb-gated progenitor-state switch: MTF2 (a PRC2 accessory subunit, co-targeting CBX2 and the INK4A/ARF locus CDKN2A) and PBX1 (co-targeting CDKN2A/CDKN2B while holding the stemness/progenitor genes NANOG, SOX3 and NOTCH3) keep a lineage-progenitor identity silenced-for-exit, opposed by the differentiation-driving arm THRB and ESRRG (which pulls in PPARGC1A/PPARGC1B, the mitochondrial-maturation coactivators, plus CDKN1A/CDKN1B), with INSM1 (NEUROD1, PAX6) and TOX (OMP) marking the neurogenic/postmitotic maturation step at the far end of that switch.
role_in_a: In head and neck carcinoma this switch is expected to run stuck in the progenitor position: Polycomb (MTF2) and PBX1 silence CDKN2A/CDKN2B and hold stemness genes (NANOG, SOX3, NOTCH3) on, while THRB and ESRRG — thyroid-hormone and orphan nuclear-receptor drivers of terminal squamous/neuroendocrine differentiation, frequently epigenetically silenced in carcinoma — fail to resolve it, sustaining a proliferative, undifferentiated tumor population.
role_in_b: In multiple sclerosis the same switch is expected to fail in oligodendrocyte precursor cells: MTF2/PBX1-held CDKN2A repression should lift as OPCs senesce in chronic lesions, THRB's classic T3-driven differentiation signal (paired with ESRRG/PPARGC1A-supported mitochondrial maturation) does not complete the transition to myelinating oligodendrocytes, and the INSM1-NEUROD1-PAX6/TOX neurogenic-maturation step stalls — a recognized contributor to remyelination failure.
shared_axis: Both tissues carry a lineage-restricted progenitor pool (OPCs in white matter; basal/squamous or neuroendocrine-transdifferentiated progenitors in head and neck epithelium) whose exit from the progenitor state is gated by the same Polycomb/nuclear-receptor module; disease in each case reflects that gate failing to resolve toward differentiation, in one case as senescent arrest (MS) and in the other as sustained self-renewal (HNC), rather than any direct anatomical or clinical connection between the two conditions.
reasoning: The six factors form a genuinely nameable module — Polycomb/stemness (MTF2, PBX1 both hitting CDKN2A) opposed by nuclear-receptor/neurogenic differentiation drivers (THRB, ESRRG, INSM1, TOX) — and each disease is separately and independently plausible for a differentiation-arrest mechanism of this general type. But none of these six carrying factors has a retrieved paper that places it in either disease, so the connection rests on the target-gene architecture and general biology of the module, not on anything in the retrieved record; the two placing citations that do exist belong to discordant factors excluded from the module.
support: none found for the carrying factors (MTF2, PBX1, THRB, ESRRG, INSM1, TOX) — no retrieved paper places any of them in either disease. Two placing citations exist but belong to discordant, excluded factors: PMID 29123999 places CEBPB in oral squamous cell carcinoma (surgical-margin inflammation genes), and PMID 39937646 places KLF4 in multiple sclerosis (neuronal rejuvenation against inflammation-mediated death); neither bears on the THRB/MTF2/ESRRG/PBX1/INSM1/TOX programme.
how_to_falsify: Take OPCs from actively remyelinating vs. chronically demyelinated MS lesions, and tumor vs. adjacent normal epithelium from HNC, and profile MTF2/PBX1 occupancy (CUT&RUN) at CDKN2A together with expression of NANOG/SOX3/NOTCH3 against induction of THRB/ESRRG target genes (PPARGC1A, CDKN1A) over a differentiation time-course; if CDKN2A/stemness-gene silencing does not move inversely with THRB/ESRRG target induction in both tissues, the shared switch does not exist as proposed.
caveats: Brain and head/neck are anatomically unrelated tissues, and the pairing is built on only 3 independent cohort pairs — the 1196 patient-group comparisons are mostly clinical subgroup splits within those 3 cohorts, not independent replications, so the ~35% concordance rate (419/1196 for the strongest factors) is more modest than the raw comparison count suggests. SP100, though concordant, was left out of the module: its targets (PLAU, MMP1, ETS1) point to an invasion/ECM-remodeling function rather than the progenitor-differentiation axis the other five factors share. CEBPB, KLF4, MYOG, ZFPM2 and KLF12 were discordant (opposite regulatory direction between the two diseases) and are excluded on that basis. The tissue-generic exclusion list (EBF1, TCF4, MEF2C, SOX10, STAT4, etc.) rules out this being a generic brain/immune signature, but it also removes several factors that would otherwise be the obvious anchors for a neural-differentiation story, which is part of why the account here leans on a smaller, less classically 'neural' set of TFs.
